title: Recovering a finite cut from its compatible complement
as_he_states: For finite compatible subsets T of a set L equipped with a reflexive symmetric compatibility relation, put C(T)={x outside T: x compatible with every t in T}. The marginal assertion is that C(T) determines T, and C(T)⊆C(T′) implies T′⊆T. The offered argument assumes compatibility of a selected t∈T′ with T, which the bare data do not ensure.
plausible_today: Additional axioms must make the complement operation injective; bare reflexive symmetric compatibility does not.
state_of_art: The three-vertex counterexample is checked in this run. No exact external fate found in S03,S06; it does not refute any later strengthened network axioms.
why_open: The page writes Oui and starts a proof; its selected point need not be compatible with the other cut. No historical explanation for the gap located.
worth: Yes, as a bounded axiomatic audit: determine precisely which cutting axiom supplies the missing compatibility.

title: Recovering all cutting data from two-point cuts
as_he_states: Boundary and finite-cut equivalence data should follow from the two-point cutting data in the proposed network axioms.
plausible_today: For dense globally bidirected posets, pair-cut data determine order up to reversal; the general network assertion requires a complete axiom system.
state_of_art: Hua2026 §78 is the exact ordered-case match; Courcelle2020 Thm3.5 covers a different finite/countable reconstruction criterion.
why_open: III4 calls this a prediction; III41 declines to complete the axiom exercise.
worth: Yes, only after fixing the intended network axioms; the ordered reconstruction itself is settled.

title: Provisional finiteness of cutting components
as_he_states: The Dec finiteness requirements may be provisional.
plausible_today: The discrete model satisfies the finite-component requirement exactly when L is finite; alternative infinitary categories should state the changed axiom.
state_of_art: No exact later adoption or rejection of these specific requirements was located (S03,S06).
why_open: The author explicitly reserves the finiteness assumptions at III6; no later historical explanation located.
worth: Moderate interest: first compare infinitary examples against each separate finiteness clause.

title: Intrinsic axioms for betweenness and pair-cut networks
as_he_states: Find conditions on R(a,b,c), or on S0 and the RE, that are equivalent to a biordered tronçon structure.
plausible_today: An exact characterization must include global bidirectedness, density and stability under nonempty strict cones, and must specify strict versus non-strict betweenness.
state_of_art: Courcelle2020 Thm3.6 concerns monadic-second-order definability for finite/countable poset betweenness; Bankston2013 treats a different road relation. Neither supplies this exact tronçon characterization. Hua2026 §78 excludes it.
why_open: III17 asks to expliciter; III41 leaves the exercise unfinished and conjectures a classical attribution to Hilbert.
worth: Yes: a finite list of relational axioms with a reconstruction proof would clarify what the network remembers.

title: T0 and sobriety of the canonical tronçon topology
as_he_states: Is every abstract tronçon T0, or sober, in its canonical topology?
plausible_today: Both fail under the displayed abstract axioms; the Q×{0,1} twin construction is a tronçon with indistinguishable generic points. The represented ficelle case is a different statement.
state_of_art: Current-run counterexample with every order/cone condition checked; no exact external resolution located (S04,S06,S07).
why_open: III23 explicitly distinguishes the ficelle assertion from the unknown general case.
worth: Yes, for identifying a separation axiom compatible with intended geometric examples.

title: Does closedness of points force a total order?
as_he_states: For totally ordered L points are closed; is the converse true?
plausible_today: No: R² with equality-or-strict-coordinate order has Euclidean strict-interval topology and is not totally ordered.
state_of_art: Independent current-run proof; general lattice interval topologies in Birkhoff are different constructions.
why_open: The parenthesized converse at III23 has no answer on the pages.
worth: Low priority after the counterexample; useful as a warning against identifying abstract tronçons with lines.

title: Closing strict intervals in the augmented topology
as_he_states: After adding complements of closed intervals/rays, do closures of strict intervals/rays equal the corresponding closed pieces, with the stated endpoint exclusions?
plausible_today: These equalities require a separate proof or counterexample; failure of the sufficient neighborhood lemma alone does not settle them.
state_of_art: No exact matching theorem located; the manuscript itself refutes the proposed neighborhood lemma in a ficelle example (III24–25).
why_open: The author abandons ordinary topology after the failed local argument.
worth: Yes, but only for a precisely fixed topology; first test the actual closure equalities on the depicted ficelle.

title: Recovering moderation from the inclusion order
as_he_states: Is {X,Y} moderated iff X∧Y exists?
plausible_today: Meet existence cannot detect compatibility in arbitrary partial Boolean algebras; the specific Mod(L) realization remains to be tested.
state_of_art: KS-1 supplies the partial-Boolean setting; a horizontal sum of two four-element Boolean blocks has incompatible atoms with meet0. No tronçon-realized counterexample is claimed.
why_open: III32 marks the equivalence with multiple question marks.
worth: Yes: begin with actual non-total tronçons before passing to arbitrary partial algebras.

title: Clopen elements universally compatible
as_he_states: Every clopen moderated element should be compatible with every element; then clopens would form a Boolean algebra.
plausible_today: False from the abstract closure axioms alone: take a non-Boolean partial Boolean algebra with identity closure. A geometric realization may impose more.
state_of_art: Pre-1986 partial Boolean algebra supplies explicit abstract models; no exact external treatment of the closure enrichment found (S04,S08,S09).
why_open: III37 says On s’attend and makes the component definition conditional.
worth: Yes, as an axiom-minimization question; identify the precise geometric property absent from the abstract axioms.

title: Endpoint check in moderated component closure
as_he_states: Check the nonclosed endpoint case in the identification of the moderated closure of a component with its closed hull.
plausible_today: For the designated finite-endpoint moderated calculus, the hull is obtained by adding the omitted remembered endpoints; this is not topological closure in the abandoned topology.
state_of_art: The endpoint argument is checked directly here; no separate later exact theorem located in S04,S08.
why_open: III39 ends the endpoint check with an ellipsis.
worth: Low priority: resolve the endpoint convention on the scans and make this local argument explicit.

title: Canonical completion of a refinement
as_he_states: Does adjoining closures of connected components of complement regions complete a refinement to a subdivision?
plausible_today: Existence of some compatible refinement does not prove this canonical recipe; tameness/local-finiteness and frontier control must be checked.
state_of_art: Esquisse1984 §§5–6 is contextual; modern stratification quotient results do not prove the recipe. No exact external theorem located (S05,S07,S09).
why_open: IV17 explicitly says that stratification conditions remain to be proved and il y a un pb.
worth: Yes: test the recipe on a fully specified low-dimensional topological example before axiomatizing it.

title: Recovering relations from the shadows of places
as_he_states: Recover refinement and compatibility of multistrata from their closed/open shadows on places; make shadow monotonicity strict and residual shadows disjoint.
plausible_today: Conditional shadow representation works inside a figure under finite-dimensional descent and nonempty disjoint residuals; it fails globally for the intended cord objects.
state_of_art: No exact external classification found; IV32–33 is an internal rejection. Modern spatial representations cannot simply replace this question.
why_open: The cord contains endpoint places differently from a simple subset, causing the author to restart.
worth: Yes, as a historical comparison with IX’s revised spatial construction, preserving the changed objects.

title: Axioms for finite compatible lower families
as_he_states: Which conditions on order and compatibility ensure the finite closed compatible subsets satisfy the figure axioms?
plausible_today: Require hereditary compatibility and finite principal lower sets, then finite compatible lower sets yield the stated finite model.
state_of_art: Classical lower-set constructions provide the elementary proof; no exact independent later multistratum formulation located (S01,S06,S10).
why_open: IV35 asks; IV36 supplies the finite-principal-set condition.
worth: Low priority: expose the equivalence as a short verified construction, keeping the dimension condition distinct.

title: Validity of Cont4 prime in non-set models
as_he_states: Check the stronger overlap/compatibility criterion in the forthcoming non-set examples.
plausible_today: No universal assertion beyond the stated conditional axiom is justified; the later cord obstruction prevents a naive set interpretation.
state_of_art: No exact external fate located; Malgoire2002 is a description, not a proof.
why_open: IV31 explicitly defers the check; IV32 changes the model.
worth: Moderate interest only after the intended cord or pseudodisk category is specified.

title: Inheritance by subcontrées
as_he_states: Do the axioms pass to refinement-closed subcontrées, and should their closure under compatible joins be finite or arbitrary?
plausible_today: Each axiom must be tested separately; the early restricted package is hereditary, while infinitary joins need a declared completion.
state_of_art: No exact external theorem for all changing axiom lists located; finite and arbitrary-join closures agree in finite systems.
why_open: Concern at IV33, proposition at38, renewed reservation at72.
worth: Yes: a version-by-version inheritance table is a practical prerequisite for examples.

title: Optional shadow criterion for disjointness
as_he_states: Should empty overlap plus compatibility of all places imply disjointness, and is this an optional axiom?
plausible_today: Empty shadows alone do not encode compatibility; retain the explicit compatibility condition or add a spatial separation hypothesis.
state_of_art: No exact matching external result located (S03,S06,S10); polarity theory alone is insufficient.
why_open: IV40 labels Cont6 Facultatif?.
worth: Yes: test whether intended geometric models satisfy the strengthened spatial separation condition.

title: Maximal refinement and subdivision
as_he_states: Prove point-extension compatibility and the existence/uniqueness of least target strata; determine whether maximality gives the displayed residual-shadow inclusion.
plausible_today: These conclusions require the added Cont6/7/8 restrictions; they are not consequences of the earlier refinement relation alone.
state_of_art: No exact external fate for this older axiom version located. V gives a concrete preorder model with proofs.
why_open: IV42 says il faut un axiome; IV43 says something is missing.
worth: Moderate interest: compare the old axioms with the sufficient set-model conditions.

title: Boundary replacement and extension of subdivisions
as_he_states: A subdivision prescribed on a subfigure should extend to the whole figure, and compatible induced refinements should agree.
plausible_today: The explicit family G′∪(F minus G) is invalid for abstract augmented strata but valid for V’s concrete subsets; the abstract theorem is existential and may replace larger strata.
state_of_art: No exact later theorem for the abstract package located; V30–45 is the internal concrete repair.
why_open: IV45–48 exposes the boundary obstruction and explicitly corrects the construction.
worth: Yes: construct one fully specified non-set model in which the existential extension axiom can be verified.

title: Consequences of the third axiom system
as_he_states: The older Cont4 relation should already follow from the C axioms (je crois).
plausible_today: Derivability must use the precise preceding C1–C7 package; it cannot be transferred to the stripped two-order list without rechecking.
state_of_art: No exact external axiom-equivalence theorem located in S07,S10.
why_open: IV53 qualifies the assertion; IV86 later questions missing hypotheses.
worth: Yes, as a finite formal dependency audit rather than a new geometric theorem.

title: Irreducibles and set representation
as_he_states: Represent figures by their irreducible strata with joins becoming unions, and recover the multistrata bijectively from a subset family.
plausible_today: Use completely join-prime generators and a separating family. Ordinary irreducibility and the displayed a,b,c do not suffice.
state_of_art: M3 and the two-point nonseparating family are checked here; VI12 supplies the exact join-prime strengthening. Birkhoff1948 is the classical representation context.
why_open: The displayed IV proof omits these distinctions; no historical reason is asserted.
worth: Yes: necessary for a reliable companion text and for distinguishing the IV and VI axiom systems.

title: Existence of connected components and global component figures
as_he_states: Does every nonempty figure have a component, and when does a component of the whole multistratum poset itself define a figure?
plausible_today: Poset comparison components exist; C4 puts each inside a figure, and C4bis governs unrestricted assembly. Finite joins yield only finite support across components.
state_of_art: The finite-space comparison-component argument is standard (ST-1); no exact external infinitary figure completion located.
why_open: IV63 crosses the first doubt; IV65 introduces the extra assumption.
worth: Low priority mathematically, but essential to avoid an unjustified full-product claim.

title: Booleanity of virtual supports
as_he_states: The biorthogonal virtual-support lattice should be a complete Boolean algebra and yield an ultrastonian space.
plausible_today: It is generally a complete ortholattice, with Booleanity requiring additional distributivity.
state_of_art: Hua2026 §79 is an exact negative answer; this run verifies the full finite figure hypotheses in seven- and ten-element models.
why_open: IV69 states the presumption and the missing distributive identity; no historical account of abandonment located.
worth: Yes: characterize additional geometric axioms forcing distributivity, rather than reproving the false conjecture.

title: Common subdivisions and a stronger moderation axiom
as_he_states: The common-subdivision property should be strengthened for moderated contrées.
plausible_today: A precise finite diagram/coherence axiom must be selected; generic triangulation analogies do not determine it.
state_of_art: Esquisse1984 §§5–6 supplies related tame stratification aims, not this exact common-refinement axiom.
why_open: IV70 says further strengthening will be needed but does not give it.
worth: Yes, after a non-set example is fixed; first state the smallest common-refinement diagram it satisfies.

title: Antisymmetry of refinement
as_he_states: Show the generated refinement preorder is an order, perhaps by an extra axiom.
plausible_today: C8 gives the needed interaction; equality of virtual supports alone cannot imply equality of subfigures.
state_of_art: The two-element chain counterexample to support separation is checked here; no exact external two-order theorem located.
why_open: IV74–76 finds the gap and proceeds without antisymmetry; IV82–84 revises C8.
worth: Yes: isolate the exact additional axiom and its necessity on small finite models.

title: Induced refinements as infima and empty infimum
as_he_states: An induced refinement should be the infimum for refinement; its emptiness should detect disjointness.
plausible_today: The old proof uses restriction and extension axioms; the converse emptiness/disjointness criterion remains an extra condition.
state_of_art: V28–30 verifies the infimum in the set/preorder model. No exact external theorem for the stripped abstract axioms found (S07,S10).
why_open: IV77 marks the emptiness direction uncertain; the proof at79 is abandoned in favor of IV52.
worth: Yes: separate existence, the universal property, and disjointness detection into independently tested statements.

title: Least target stratum and admissible multi-shadows
as_he_states: Find the least target stratum of a refining elementary figure, then prove admissibility of all closed shadows.
plausible_today: Leastness follows with the stated descent/restriction conditions; admissibility additionally requires nonempty residual shadows and separation.
state_of_art: V1–4 and VIII37 offer the internal set-family criterion. No general later theorem identified in the searched literature.
why_open: IV80 assumes finite combinatorial dimension; IV89 notes a previously used axiom.
worth: Yes: write an exact implication chain and locate where each shadow axiom enters.

title: Minimal axioms for the two-order calculus
as_he_states: Separate conditions for existence of induced refinements from conditions making them commute with induction; find minimal axioms.
plausible_today: A useful formulation should include finite subfigure meets and the necessary interchange/extension axioms; minimality remains open in this dossier.
state_of_art: No exact matching factorization theorem located in S07,S10; category-theoretic similarity alone is insufficient.
why_open: IV86 explicitly asks whether hypotheses are missing.
worth: High interest: finite model search can rapidly separate independent axioms without developing a whole geometry.

title: Places, elementary figures and subdivision-minimality
as_he_states: Characterize places as minimal figures; the converse should hold for ball-like objects.
plausible_today: Refinement-minimal nonempty figures are elementary and subfigure-minimal. No proper subdivision is a weaker condition; the claimed ball case needs a geometric model.
state_of_art: No exact external ball-case theorem located; identity subdivision supplies the abstract distinction.
why_open: IV88 says the converse is false in the current system and reserves a geometric case.
worth: Yes, once ball-like figures are defined precisely; otherwise the converse has no fixed scope.

title: Independence of pre-admissibility conditions
as_he_states: Determine equivalences among residual partition, intersection and saturation conditions; the first finite independence example is rejected.
plausible_today: Membership coverage β is indispensable in infinite families; VIII44–45 provides the corrected infinite example.
state_of_art: The standard Alexandrov viewpoint explains the least-member condition; no exact external statement of this redundancy taxonomy located (S01,S04,S06).
why_open: V4 calls the attempted example idiot and points to VIII.
worth: Low priority: retain the corrected infinite example and separate pre-admissibility from nonempty residuals.

title: Compatibility equivalences and local finiteness
as_he_states: Complete the remaining directions of the compatibility proposition; determine stability of allowed geometric subfamilies under joins.
plausible_today: The four compatibility criteria hold for admissible families; local-finiteness restrictions are generally stable under finite, not arbitrary, joins.
state_of_art: Direct proof in the manuscript checked here; modern Alexandrov representation is background (WWY-1). No exact external multistratum formulation located.
why_open: V8–10 completes the proof; V18–19 qualifies the global restrictions.
worth: Low priority: present the complete equivalence and preserve the finite-join qualification.

title: Recovering subfigure inclusion from refinement and subdivision
as_he_states: Can ≤ be expressed using ≪ and ≼ alone?
plausible_today: The stated necessary condition (a subfigure that subdivides is equal) does not supply a definition of ≤. A reconstruction theorem or two nonisomorphic subfigure orders with the same remaining data is needed.
state_of_art: No exact matching result found (S03,S06,S10).
why_open: V27 asks directly and gives only necessary conditions.
worth: High interest: finite admissible-family systems give concrete data for a reconstruction or counterexample search.

title: Restriction and extension axioms C6/C7 in the set model
as_he_states: Verify uniqueness of induced subfigures and extension of a prescribed subdivision.
plausible_today: Both hold for admissible subset families; extension is realized by the least finer topology on a fixed closed support.
state_of_art: The manuscript proves these through V45; the least-extension proof is independently checked here. Searches S04,S05,S08,S10 found no exact external historical match.
why_open: V27 defers them; V30–32 proves construction and V40–45 supplies the topology argument.
worth: Moderate interest as a clean self-contained theorem, with the abstract-model limitation made explicit.

title: Characterizing the least extension by its outside strata
as_he_states: Conditions b,c,d should be equivalent and should characterize the least extension.
plausible_today: The common-closed-stratum lemma and d⇒b,c are false; b⇔c survives. The four weak topological tests are insufficient. Preserving closures of every subset outside the closed locus is the correct condition.
state_of_art: Two-point counterexample to the additional lemma and the author’s three-point counterexample are independently certified. Borges1967 does not prove the false characterization.
why_open: The leastness implication is explicitly retracted at V43,48–49; the separate common-stratum gap is not retracted in these cotes.
worth: Yes: the two distinct failures must be separated before restating the extension theorem.

title: Universal property of lower-ideal replacement
as_he_states: State the poset replacement separately and use its terminal property to infer leastness.
plausible_today: The replacement is terminal among diagrams preserving the specified lower part and complement identification; this does not force arbitrary bijective outside maps to be isomorphisms.
state_of_art: Direct order proof checked; standard Alexandrov functoriality is background. No exact external historical match for this presentation located.
why_open: V36 asks for a separate proposition; V37’s hoped-for stronger inference is later retracted.
worth: Moderate interest: write the correct diagram category and universal property explicitly.

title: Least finer topology extending a closed-subspace topology
as_he_states: Construct the least finer topology, describe closed sets and closures, and establish the converse characterization.
plausible_today: For closed T⊂S and σ finer than τ|T, closed sets are A∪B with A τ-closed, B σ-closed in T; closure is clτ(X∩U)∪clσ(X∩T).
state_of_art: Full direct proof checked below. Borges1967 treats related simple extensions but no exact matching result was located. The final displayed intersection is a reading alarm.
why_open: A cancelled distributive expansion is replaced by a general proof; the weak converse is refuted and corrected at V49.
worth: Yes for exposition and reuse; its elementary general proof is complete, so a research task should focus on historical attribution or extensions.

title: Homotopical properties of the replacement map
as_he_states: Quotient, connected-fiber, contractible-fiber and homotopically proper universal weak-equivalence properties should pass from the replaced locus to the whole map.
plausible_today: Quotientness, point-fiber assertions and principal-lower-ideal contractibility pass as stated. The universal claim needs a precise definition of properness and allowed base changes.
state_of_art: Quillen1973 Theorem A exactly covers the principal-ideal criterion; it does not establish the unqualified universal assertion.
why_open: V47 supplies a greatest-element argument but leaves the stronger terminology implicit. No historical explanation is claimed.
worth: Yes: fix the intended homotopical-properness definition before testing universal base change.
